label: Nginx Proxy Manager

sensitivePaths.label: Change the password of a Nginx Proxy Manager account
sensitivePaths.warning: If this is the account this connection uses, Allkin will lose access to the service as soon as the current token expires — and so will you, if you do not know the new password.

sensitivePaths.label: Delete a Nginx Proxy Manager account
sensitivePaths.warning: Deleting the last administrator makes the interface unreachable.

sensitivePaths.label: Create a Nginx Proxy Manager account
sensitivePaths.warning: An account created here can be given administration rights over the whole proxy.

sensitivePaths.label: Change the rights of an account
Change the configuration of Nginx Proxy Manager
sensitivePaths.warning: The settings include what the server answers for an unknown domain: a change here applies to all the traffic, not to one host.

sensitivePaths.label: Delete a certificate
sensitivePaths.warning: Every host that uses it loses HTTPS: browsers will show a security warning until another certificate is attached to them.

sensitivePaths.label: Request a certificate
sensitivePaths.warning: Let's Encrypt allows 5 identical certificates per week and 50 per domain: a repeated failure burns the quota of the domain for seven days. The request also disables, while the validation runs, the hosts that carry these domains.

sensitivePaths.label: Replace a certificate with a file
Open a TCP/UDP stream
sensitivePaths.warning: The port is relayed as it is to the internal machine, with neither filtering nor encryption.

sensitivePaths.label: Publish a service on the Internet
sensitivePaths.warning: The domain becomes reachable from outside and points to the internal machine given. Check the pair domain → host:port before accepting.

sensitivePaths.label: Change a published service
sensitivePaths.warning: A domain already in service may end up pointing elsewhere.

sensitivePaths.label: Change an access list
sensitivePaths.warning: An access list protects several hosts at once: changing it affects them all.

sensitivePaths.label: Disable a host
sensitivePaths.warning: The domain stops answering until it is enabled again.

sensitivePaths.label: Delete an entry of the proxy
sensitivePaths.warning: The configuration is erased, not disabled: it will have to be redone entirely.

agentGuide:
Nginx Proxy Manager (NPM): the reverse proxy that puts the services of a machine behind a domain name and a certificate. The base URL ends with /api; you then give paths such as /nginx/proxy-hosts. Allkin opens the session and sets the token — NEVER call /tokens yourself, you have neither the e-mail address nor the password.

SIX FAMILIES, all built alike — GET (list), POST (create), then GET/PUT/DELETE /{id}:
· /nginx/proxy-hosts — a domain to an internal service. The heart of it.
· /nginx/redirection-hosts — a domain to another URL.
· /nginx/dead-hosts — a domain that answers 404 on purpose.
· /nginx/streams — a TCP/UDP port relayed as it is.
· /nginx/access-lists — a password or an IP filter, reusable by several hosts.
· /nginx/certificates — the certificates.
The four families of hosts also have POST /{id}/enable and POST /{id}/disable.

READING. GET /nginx/proxy-hosts returns EVERYTHING, and it is verbose: use "extract". extract="[].domain_names" for the names, "[enabled=1].domain_names" for the active ones, "[id=7]" for a single one. Better still, filter on the server: ?query=example.com only returns the hosts one of whose domains contains that text — nothing superfluous leaves, so nothing is paid for. ?expand=certificate,owner,access_list joins the linked objects. GET /reports/hosts gives the counters, GET /audit-log who changed what, GET / the version (the only public call).

PUBLISHING A SERVICE — the common case:
POST /nginx/proxy-hosts
body {"domain_names":["app.example.com"],"forward_scheme":"http","forward_host":"192.168.1.10","forward_port":8080}
These four fields are required. Respect the TYPES: forward_port is an integer (8080, not "8080") and domain_names an array, even for a single name. Useful options: block_exploits, allow_websocket_upgrade, caching_enabled, http2_support, ssl_forced, access_list_id, advanced_config (a raw nginx block), locations (sub-paths to other targets).
NPM refuses a domain already taken by any type of host: "<name> is already in use". List before creating.

THE CERTIFICATE. Two ways:
· in one go: add "certificate_id": "new" to the POST of the host, NPM asks for the certificate right after;
· separately: POST /nginx/certificates with {"provider":"letsencrypt","domain_names":["app.example.com"],"meta":{"dns_challenge":false}}, then "certificate_id": <id> on the host.
The e-mail address is the one of the NPM account: there is no field to provide for it. Let's Encrypt must be able to reach the domain over HTTP on port 80 from the Internet — otherwise go through "dns_challenge": true, which asks for dns_provider and dns_provider_credentials (see GET /nginx/certificates/dns-providers).

CHANGING. PUT /{id} is a PARTIAL adjustment: send only the fields that change, not the whole object.

DIAGNOSING. The field meta of a host carries nginx_online and nginx_err: that is where a refused configuration is read, not in the HTTP code of your request — a host can be created (201) and broken. Two codes of NPM to read the other way round: a 500 "Internal Error" on a call that used to work means an expired token, simply make the call again; a 404 on a path that exists means the request left without a token. In both cases the path is right, do not look for another.

WHAT GOES THROUGH THE USER: publishing, changing or deleting a host, disabling a host, asking for or deleting a certificate, opening a stream, touching the accounts or the settings. It is not a refusal — say what you are about to do, the user accepts, the call goes again. Listing and diagnosing stay free.

FOR THE REST: GET /schema returns the complete OpenAPI of THIS installation. It weighs about 260 KB, so never go there without extract — for instance extract="paths./nginx/streams" for the one family you are interested in.

sensitivePaths.label: Changer le mot de passe d'un compte Nginx Proxy Manager
sensitivePaths.warning: Si c'est le compte que cette connexion utilise, Allkin perdra l'accès au service dès l'expiration du jeton en cours — et vous aussi, si vous ne connaissez pas le nouveau mot de passe.

sensitivePaths.label: Supprimer un compte Nginx Proxy Manager
sensitivePaths.warning: Supprimer le dernier administrateur rend l'interface inaccessible.

sensitivePaths.label: Créer un compte Nginx Proxy Manager
sensitivePaths.warning: Un compte créé ici peut recevoir les droits d'administration sur tout le proxy.

sensitivePaths.label: Modifier la configuration de Nginx Proxy Manager
sensitivePaths.warning: Les réglages incluent ce que répond le serveur pour un domaine inconnu : un changement ici vaut pour tout le trafic, pas pour un hôte.

sensitivePaths.label: Supprimer un certificat
sensitivePaths.warning: Tous les hôtes qui s'en servent perdent le HTTPS : les navigateurs afficheront une alerte de sécurité jusqu'à ce qu'un autre certificat leur soit attaché.

sensitivePaths.label: Demander un certificat
sensitivePaths.warning: Let's Encrypt limite à 5 certificats identiques par semaine et 50 par domaine : un échec répété grille le quota du domaine pour sept jours. La demande désactive aussi, le temps de la validation, les hôtes qui portent ces domaines.

sensitivePaths.label: Remplacer un certificat par un fichier
Ouvrir un flux TCP/UDP
sensitivePaths.warning: Le port est relayé tel quel vers la machine interne, sans filtrage ni chiffrement.

sensitivePaths.label: Publier un service sur Internet
sensitivePaths.warning: Le domaine devient joignable depuis l'extérieur et pointe vers la machine interne indiquée. Vérifiez le couple domaine → hôte:port avant d'accepter.

sensitivePaths.label: Modifier un service publié
sensitivePaths.warning: Un domaine déjà en service peut se retrouver dirigé ailleurs.

sensitivePaths.label: Modifier une liste d'accès
sensitivePaths.warning: Une liste d'accès protège plusieurs hôtes à la fois : la modifier les touche tous.

sensitivePaths.label: Désactiver un hôte
sensitivePaths.warning: Le domaine cesse de répondre jusqu'à réactivation.

sensitivePaths.label: Supprimer une entrée du proxy
sensitivePaths.warning: La configuration est effacée, pas désactivée : elle sera à refaire entièrement.

sensitivePaths.label: Cambiar la contraseña de una cuenta de Nginx Proxy Manager
sensitivePaths.warning: Si es la cuenta que usa esta conexión, Allkin perderá el acceso al servicio en cuanto caduque el token actual; y tú también, si no conoces la nueva contraseña.

sensitivePaths.label: Eliminar una cuenta de Nginx Proxy Manager
sensitivePaths.warning: Eliminar al último administrador deja la interfaz inaccesible.

sensitivePaths.label: Crear una cuenta de Nginx Proxy Manager
sensitivePaths.warning: Una cuenta creada aquí puede recibir permisos de administración sobre todo el proxy.

sensitivePaths.label: Modificar los permisos de una cuenta
Modificar la configuración de Nginx Proxy Manager
sensitivePaths.warning: Los ajustes incluyen lo que responde el servidor para un dominio desconocido: un cambio aquí vale para todo el tráfico, no para un host.

sensitivePaths.label: Eliminar un certificado
sensitivePaths.warning: Todos los hosts que lo usan pierden el HTTPS: los navegadores mostrarán una alerta de seguridad hasta que se les asocie otro certificado.

sensitivePaths.label: Solicitar un certificado
sensitivePaths.warning: Let's Encrypt limita a 5 certificados idénticos por semana y 50 por dominio: un fallo repetido agota la cuota del dominio durante siete días. La solicitud también desactiva, mientras dura la validación, los hosts que llevan esos dominios.

sensitivePaths.label: Reemplazar un certificado por un archivo
Abrir un flujo TCP/UDP
sensitivePaths.warning: El puerto se reenvía tal cual a la máquina interna, sin filtrado ni cifrado.

sensitivePaths.label: Publicar un servicio en Internet
sensitivePaths.warning: El dominio pasa a ser accesible desde el exterior y apunta a la máquina interna indicada. Comprueba el par dominio → host:puerto antes de aceptar.

sensitivePaths.label: Modificar un servicio publicado
sensitivePaths.warning: Un dominio ya en servicio puede acabar apuntando a otro sitio.

sensitivePaths.label: Modificar una lista de acceso
sensitivePaths.warning: Una lista de acceso protege varios hosts a la vez: modificarla los afecta a todos.

sensitivePaths.label: Desactivar un host
sensitivePaths.warning: El dominio deja de responder hasta que se reactive.

sensitivePaths.label: Eliminar una entrada del proxy
sensitivePaths.warning: La configuración se borra, no se desactiva: habrá que rehacerla por completo.

sensitivePaths.label: Passwort eines Nginx-Proxy-Manager-Kontos ändern
sensitivePaths.warning: Wenn es das Konto ist, das diese Verbindung nutzt, verliert Allkin den Zugriff auf den Dienst, sobald das aktuelle Token abläuft – und du auch, wenn du das neue Passwort nicht kennst.

sensitivePaths.label: Nginx-Proxy-Manager-Konto löschen
sensitivePaths.warning: Wird der letzte Administrator gelöscht, ist die Oberfläche nicht mehr erreichbar.

sensitivePaths.label: Nginx-Proxy-Manager-Konto erstellen
sensitivePaths.warning: Ein hier erstelltes Konto kann Administrationsrechte für den gesamten Proxy erhalten.

sensitivePaths.label: Konfiguration von Nginx Proxy Manager ändern
sensitivePaths.warning: Die Einstellungen legen auch fest, was der Server bei einer unbekannten Domain antwortet: Eine Änderung hier gilt für den gesamten Datenverkehr, nicht für einen Host.

sensitivePaths.label: Zertifikat löschen
sensitivePaths.warning: Alle Hosts, die es nutzen, verlieren HTTPS: Browser zeigen eine Sicherheitswarnung, bis ihnen ein anderes Zertifikat zugewiesen wird.

sensitivePaths.label: Zertifikat anfordern
sensitivePaths.warning: Let's Encrypt erlaubt 5 identische Zertifikate pro Woche und 50 pro Domain: Wiederholte Fehlschläge verbrauchen das Kontingent der Domain für sieben Tage. Die Anforderung deaktiviert außerdem während der Validierung die Hosts, die diese Domains tragen.

sensitivePaths.label: TCP/UDP-Stream öffnen
sensitivePaths.warning: Der Port wird unverändert an die interne Maschine weitergeleitet, ohne Filterung und ohne Verschlüsselung.

sensitivePaths.label: Dienst im Internet veröffentlichen
sensitivePaths.warning: Die Domain wird von außen erreichbar und zeigt auf die angegebene interne Maschine. Prüfe das Paar Domain → Host:Port, bevor du zustimmst.

sensitivePaths.label: Veröffentlichten Dienst ändern
sensitivePaths.warning: Eine bereits genutzte Domain kann danach woandershin zeigen.

sensitivePaths.label: Zugriffsliste ändern
sensitivePaths.warning: Eine Zugriffsliste schützt mehrere Hosts zugleich: Eine Änderung betrifft sie alle.

sensitivePaths.label: Host deaktivieren
sensitivePaths.warning: Die Domain antwortet nicht mehr, bis sie wieder aktiviert wird.

sensitivePaths.label: Proxy-Eintrag löschen
sensitivePaths.warning: Die Konfiguration wird gelöscht, nicht deaktiviert: Sie muss vollständig neu angelegt werden.
